q: RA 4136 is also known as the:
info: RA 4136 compiles PH land transportation and traffic laws; it is the basis of most LTO exam questions.

q: Maximum speed on city and municipal streets with light traffic under RA 4136:
info: RA 4136 Sec 35 caps city/municipal streets at 30 kph; open country roads allow up to 80 kph for light vehicles.

q: Maximum speed for light vehicles on open country roads under RA 4136:
info: RA 4136 Sec 35 sets 80 kph for light vehicles on open country roads without blind corners or dense habitation.

q: Maximum speed on crowded streets under RA 4136:
info: Crowded streets limit speed to 20 kph under RA 4136 because pedestrians and hazards are dense.

q: Driving or parking on a sidewalk, path, or alley not intended for vehicles is:
info: RA 4136 bans driving or parking on sidewalks and paths not intended for vehicular traffic; they are for pedestrians.

q: Hitching a person, bicycle, or motorcycle to a moving motor vehicle is:
info: RA 4136 prohibits hitching persons or vehicles to a motor vehicle because a fall or swing causes crashes.

q: If your load extends more than 1 meter beyond the vehicle bed, you must display:
C: a red flag at least 30 cm long and wide
info: RA 4136 requires a red flag at least 30 cm long and wide on every projecting end of an over-1-meter load.

q: The color of a motor vehicle's headlights must be:
info: RA 4136 Sec 34 requires headlights in white or yellowish white for proper road illumination.

q: Taillights must be red and visible from a distance of:
info: RA 4136 Sec 34 requires red taillights visible within 100 meters so following drivers see you at night.

q: Every internal-combustion motor vehicle must have a muffler and must not emit:
C: unnecessary or disagreeable smoke or noise
info: RA 4136 mandates mufflers and bans operating a vehicle so as to make unnecessary smoke or noise.

q: Overtaking on a curve or grade when your view is obstructed within 500 feet (150 m) is:
info: LTO rules ban overtaking on curves or grades with under 500 ft (150 m) visibility; you cannot see oncoming traffic.

q: Overtaking another vehicle at an intersection is:
C: prohibited, except on multi-lane one-direction roads where you may pass on the right
info: LTO CDE rules ban intersection overtaking due to crossing conflicts, except passing on the right on 2+ lane one-way roads.

q: Overtaking at a railway grade crossing is:
A: allowed if no train is seen
info: Never overtake at a railway crossing; a stalled or slow pass in front of a train is fatal.

q: Overtaking on the right side is allowed when:
A: the vehicle ahead is visibly turning left
C: the road is a two-way single lane
info: LTO CDE allows passing on the right when the vehicle ahead is visibly turning left or on 2+ lanes in one direction.

q: Before crossing a through highway or railroad where no hazard is apparent, you may slow to:
A: 5 mph (8 kph) instead of a full stop
info: RA 4136 requires a full stop before through highways/railroads, but allows slowing to 5 mph (8 kph) when clearly no hazard exists.

q: At an intersection where vehicles go in different directions, priority goes to:
info: LTO right-of-way rules: the vehicle on the right has priority when paths cross from different directions.

q: On a steep grade where two vehicles meet and only one can pass, priority goes to:
info: LTO right-of-way rules favor the uphill vehicle, since stopping and restarting uphill is harder and riskier.

q: The LTO fine for driving without a valid driver's license is:
info: Driving without a valid license carries a standard Php 3,000 LTO fine under the traffic violation schedule.

q: The LTO fine for driving an unregistered or improperly registered motor vehicle is:
info: Unregistered operation is fined Php 10,000 against the owner; always keep registration updated.

q: The first-offense fine for reckless driving is:
info: Reckless driving (operating without reasonable caution) is fined Php 2,000 on first offense per LTO schedule.

q: Under RA 10930, a driver's license is valid for 5 years reckoned from:
info: RA 10930 sets 5-year validity counted from the licensee's birthdate, unless suspended or revoked.

q: A driver's license may be valid for 10 years upon renewal if the holder:
info: RA 10930 rewards violation-free drivers with 10-year validity on renewal; any demerit limits it to 5 years.

q: Which permit is NOT covered by the 5-year license validity under RA 10930?
info: RA 10930 expressly excludes student permits, which remain valid for only 1 year as a learning authority.

q: Under RA 10586, DUI with NO resulting injury carries 3 months imprisonment and a fine of:
info: RA 10586 punishes DUI without injury with 3 months jail plus Php 20,000–80,000; injury raises it to Php 100,000–200,000.

q: A professional driver's license is perpetually revoked on the ___ DUI conviction under RA 10586:
info: RA 10586 confiscates and perpetually revokes a professional license on the very first DUI conviction.

q: A non-professional license on first DUI conviction is suspended for:
info: RA 10586 suspends a non-pro license for 12 months on first conviction, and revokes it perpetually on the second.

q: First-offense fine under the Anti-Distracted Driving Act (RA 10913):
info: RA 10913 fines handheld-device use while driving Php 5,000 (1st), Php 10,000 (2nd), Php 15,000 + 3-month suspension (3rd).

q: Second-offense fine under RA 10913:
info: RA 10913 escalates to Php 10,000 on second offense, then Php 15,000 plus 3-month suspension on third.

q: Third-offense penalty under RA 10913:
info: A third distracted-driving offense brings Php 15,000 plus 3-month suspension; a fourth means revocation.

q: Under RA 10054, who must wear a standard protective helmet?
info: RA 10054 Motorcycle Helmet Act requires standard helmets for driver AND back rider at all times.

q: First-offense fine for not wearing a standard helmet (RA 10054):
info: RA 10054 fines helmet violations Php 1,500 (1st), Php 3,000 (2nd), Php 5,000 (3rd), Php 10,000 + confiscation after.

q: Third-offense fine for helmet violation (RA 10054):
info: Helmet fines escalate Php 1,500 → Php 3,000 → Php 5,000; a fourth costs Php 10,000 plus license confiscation.

q: Under RA 8750 Seat Belts Use Act, seatbelts are required for:
info: RA 8750 requires the driver and front-seat passengers of private and public vehicles to buckle up.

q: First-offense fine for seatbelt violation (RA 8750):
info: RA 8750 fines go Php 1,000 (1st), Php 2,000 (2nd), Php 5,000 plus suspension (3rd); driver and operator are liable.

q: Second-offense fine for seatbelt violation (RA 8750):
info: Seatbelt fines escalate Php 1,000 → Php 2,000 → Php 5,000 with suspension on subsequent offenses.

q: Third-offense penalty for violating RA 10666 (child aboard motorcycle):
info: RA 10666 third offenses bring Php 10,000 plus 1-month suspension, after Php 3,000 (1st) and Php 5,000 (2nd).

q: Motorcycles allowed on expressways must have engine displacement of:
info: Sub-400cc motorcycles are banned from expressways; only 400cc-and-above bikes have the speed and stability required.

q: Motor vehicle registration must be renewed:
info: PH registration is yearly; driving unregistered risks a Php 10,000 fine, so renew on schedule.

q: A load projecting beyond the vehicle at night must show red lights visible from at least:
info: RA 4136 requires red lights (in place of daytime red flags) visible at least 50 meters on projecting loads at night.

q: A professional license differs from non-professional because it allows driving:
info: A professional license authorizes operating vehicles for compensation or hire; non-pro is strictly private use.
